reviews.title: Shopping Links Ruin The App Experience
reviews.text:
This app used to be great, now I can’t scroll through pictures without shopping links popping up. They come up in a way that they take over your whole screen and the experience of using the app is just not what it used to be. 

What is truly frustrating is that, similar to Instagram, the Pinterest app is seemingly trying to npressure its users into shopping which allows Pinterest to get a commission on the purchases.

I can see how users may want to know where to buy something, but to take over the whole screen with pop ups and links for every single picture is just a horrible way to pressure your users into making purchases. 

If they created a setting to turn this feature off or if they made it more subtle, like you can click on something in the corner and then the links show up...this would create a much more positive user experience. 

It’s unfortunate that so many of these photo apps are now trying to push their users into spending money when people really visit these apps for inspiration and to learn how to do new things.

Pinterest, please change the setup of your shopping links.

I still agree with the above statement, however I have since deleted the app off my phone due to the AI generated content. Tolerating the shopping links and pop-ups was do-able, but the AI slop completely negates the reason this app even exists.

I understand that platforms need to generate revenue, but there’s a difference between monetisation and shoving advertisements down your users’ throats at every possible opportunity. Not every single interaction needs to be monetised. Let people enjoy the damn app.

reviews.title: Trop de publicité !
reviews.text:
J’aurais pu mettre cinq étoiles à l’époque, mais aujourd’hui, Pinterest m’a tellement dégoûtée que je ne peux mettre qu’une seule étoile.

Avant, je pouvais passer des heures entières sur Pinterest à regarder mes épingles enregistrées, à chercher de l’inspiration et à découvrir de nouvelles choses. Maintenant, si j’y passe dix minutes, c’est déjà le grand maximum. L’application n’a tout simplement plus rien de plaisant visuellement.

Il y a désormais tellement de publicités qu’on a presque l’impression de passer plus de temps à regarder des annonces qu’à profiter du contenu pour lequel on est venu. Avant, on pouvait faire défiler des dizaines d’épingles inspirantes sans être constamment interrompu. Aujourd’hui, on a l’impression que pour quatre épingles, on se retrouve avec deux publicités et deux épingles intéressantes, quand on a de la chance.

Le pire, c’est que ces publicités sont souvent totalement inintéressantes et finissent par gâcher l’expérience. On ne peut même plus se concentrer sur ce qu’on regarde tellement on est constamment sollicité. Je passe désormais mon temps à signaler les publicités pour essayer de retrouver un minimum de plaisir sur l’application, et ça devient franchement insupportable.

Pinterest était une véritable source d’inspiration. Maintenant, on dirait simplement un panneau publicitaire géant. C’est dommage d’avoir autant dégradé une application qui était autrefois aussi agréable à utiliser.

I never had it happen before but it’s suddenly started and now has given me a migraine. All this pointless wave achieves is to obscure the user ability to LOOK AT THE IMAGE which as far as I’m aware is the entire point of Pinterest. 

This particular design decision is up there with google making their search tool worse to force people to do multiple searches thereby increase ad revenues. reviews.title: Stop Removing Non-Explicit References
reviews.text:
Pinterest used to be one of the best places for artists to collect references, but the moderation has become absurd. Completely non-explicit anatomy references, shirtless male poses, and even people in underwear are being flagged as “adult content.” I spend hours carefully organizing reference boards, only to have perfectly harmless Pins removed later.

The automated moderation seems far too aggressive and doesn’t understand the difference between artistic anatomy and explicit content. If you’re going to remove Pins, at least provide a clear explanation and a reliable appeal process.

Pinterest is making itself less useful for artists, designers, and illustrators. Please fix the moderation system instead of punishing legitimate reference material.

reviews.title: Frustrated
reviews.text: Where to begin? I’ve been using this app for years and I loved it so much until about a year ago. I had tens of thousands of pins, but all of a sudden it seemed like half of all the pins I saved were ai without me realizing. I also noticed a sudden abundance in ads. Seriously, I couldn’t scroll through three pins without an ad popping up. Between the ai and ads, only really a fourth of the pins suggested to me were actually things I wanted to save. That’s not insane, considering it’s probably the same on Tiktok or other social media—but when you consider how incredibly tailored Pinterest used to be, it’s astounding. Then, like a final blow to the once incredible apps reputation in my own life, I was banned. I’ve had my account since sixth grade and had a seriously mind boggling amount of pins saved, and my account was deactivated. It should work the same as (for example) Instagram, where you can not only easily choose what folder to put it in, but if you accidentally put it in the wrong folder, you can easily unsave it straight away, whereas (on pinterest) if you accidentally save an image in the wrong board you have to go to your saved boards and delete it from there.

I come here to escape the nonsense of other social media platforms and it’s starting to annoy me just as bad as the others.
